thread:
alex: Hey team, noticed a spike of internal DNS timeouts this morning that lines up with a GPU batch job rollout to east-*-gpu-pool. Services calling internal APIs got 5xx/timeout cascades.
maria: Saw the same. Pod logs show `dial tcp: lookup svc.internal: no such host` followed by normal resolution after ~300-700ms. Not full failures but enough to blow up retries.
tim: I pulled CoreDNS metrics — no OOMs, QPS steady. But node-local-dns (daemonset) shows a pattern: a ~20s window of 100-200ms per query for a subset of nodes during burst.
infra-bot: Deploy event: rollout/ai-batch v2 -> 60 pods across east-1 gpu nodes @ 07:12 UTC :rocket:
sre-oncall: Any packet loss on the host NICs? I ran `ip -s link` on one node and saw UDP rx errors bump during the window.
alex: Grabbed a snippet from node-local-dns logs on node gpu-ew-14:
```
2026-06-12T07:12:15Z INFO cache: miss for "svc.internal.default.svc.cluster.local"
2026-06-12T07:12:15Z DEBUG upstream: query forwarded to 10.96.0.10:53
2026-06-12T07:12:15Z WARN upstream: udp read timeout after 250ms
2026-06-12T07:12:15Z INFO retrying via TCP
2026-06-12T07:12:15Z INFO served: 180ms
```
maria: Those `udp read timeout` lines correlate with logs from kube-proxy showing conntrack create/delete churning. conntrack-nf stats showed 95% usage on gpu-ew-14.
tim: I also noticed MTU fragmentation counters on the cni interface incrementing — we have some jumbo frames enabled on the east-1 GPUs (9000) while the overlay path to CoreDNS nodes is 1500. Could be UDP fragments getting dropped.
alex: Interesting — RDMA setup on those nodes sets a different path MTU in the offload table. When bursts create many short DNS queries, fragmentation + conntrack churn + node-local cache misses => latency sawtooth.
sre-oncall: Short-term mitigation I pushed: set sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 on affected nodes and decreased nf_conntrack_udp_timeout to 30s. Also applied iptables rule to clamp MSS for TCP to 1400 on the cni bridge.
maria: After the conntrack bump we saw a 60% reduction in error traces. But still intermittent ~150ms spikes while cache warms.
devex: Could we pre-warm node-local cache on rollout? Maybe have the deployment run a small prober that resolves key services before traffic hits.
tim: Good idea. Also for a medium-term fix we should fix MTU consistency across the path or disable jumbo frames on gpu nodes until the overlay supports larger MTU end-to-end.
alex: Action items:
- (tim) file an infra ticket to normalize MTU for east-1 GPU subnet and validate with `ping -s` and `tracepath` tests. (ETA 1d)
- (maria) add prober initContainer to ai-batch rollout template to prime node-local-dns cache. (ETA next deploy)
- (sre-oncall) roll the conntrack sysctl cluster-wide via machine-config for GPU pool but keep monitoring. (ETA continuous)
- (devex) write short runbook: how to rollback to using CoreDNS directly (bypass node-local) if node-local causes issues.
sre-oncall: I'll also add alerting on node-local-dns miss-rate > 5% and conntrack usage > 80% for GPU node-pools.
alex: One more note — we saw TCP fallback for queries (node-local retried via TCP) which hides absolute failures but increases tail latency. We should tune the node-local retry policy to fail fast for specific internal endpoints to avoid domino retries in the app.
maria: Confirmed no user-facing impact beyond higher internal latencies for a few minutes. Will post a short incident summary after actions.
infra-bot: Monitor rule created: node-local-dns_miss_rate / gpu-pool > 0.05 for 5m -> page SRE.
alex: Thanks all. If you find a reproducible script to simulate the burst reliably, drop it here and we can run in staging.
